To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GAV genome has two conserved intergenetic sequences, and the sgmRNAS are initiated from these sequences, but do not possess 3'-leader sequences.
the GAV genome has two conserved intergene sequences and two 3'-co-terminal sgRNAs that do initiate from these intergene sequences but do not possess 3'-genomic sequences fused to their 5'-terminus.
the gill-associated virus of Penaeusmonodonprawns transcribes 5'-coterminal sg mRNAs that lack 5'-leadersequences.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GAV has a genome of approximately 20 kb that contains only two ORFs, one for the viral replicase and one for the viral envelope glycoprotein.
GAV is a member of the order NIDOVIRALES but is a distinct virus from the other known nidoviruses.
GAV is not a coronavirus or an arterivirus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new nidovirus that infects a crustacean host and that the genome organization and transcription strategy of GAV is unique among the nidoviruses.

GAV has fewer genes than vertebrate nidoviruses.
the gill associated nidovirus of prawn is different from other nidoviruses in that it does not use a 5'-leader sequence in the production of subgenomic RNA.
